The edit is complete and the module passes a syntax check. Summary of the change:

**What I changed:** Rebuilt the wings and re-hung the engines in `plane.js` — targeting the wing_geometry criterion (Claude track's weakest at 3/10, and the subject of gemma's complaints on views 4/5/6/7: "straight rectangular slabs, no sweep or taper").

**Why:** My own inspection of view-5 (top-down) and view-1/6 confirmed the wing was a single flat `BoxGeometry(10, 0.6, 55)` slab — zero sweep, zero taper, zero dihedral, invisible edge-on in profile — with all four nacelles at one X station so profiles stacked them into "one engine block." The reference planform/three-view shows strongly swept, heavily tapered wings with nacelles below and ahead of the leading edge.

**The concrete edits (one tightly-coupled set):**
1. **Wings:** replaced the slab with two swept trapezoid surfaces using the same ExtrudeGeometry pattern already proven for the tail stabilizers — ~37.5° leading-edge sweep, root chord 15 tapering to 3.5 at the tip (taper ratio ~0.23), semi-span 27.5 (span ~55 ≈ 0.9× body length), ~6.9° dihedral, low-mounted with the root underside at y=-2.3 buried in the lower fuselage lobe and both roots meeting on the centerline so nothing floats.
2. **Engines:** the four nacelles (counts, sizes, dark inlets unchanged) now restagger along the swept leading edge at 40%/69% semi-span, each hung on a pylon under the *local* wing underside (which rises with dihedral), inlets poking ~3 units ahead of the local leading edge — so profiles now show two clearly staggered engines per side, and the top view shows nacelles ahead of a swept edge instead of stubs on a rectangle.
3. **Gear coupling fix:** the two wing-mounted main-gear strut tops moved from y=-0.1 to y=-0.8 so they stay embedded inside the new, lower wing instead of spiking through its top surface.
